title: Any client can read all customers' personal data through the admin customers list
summary: GET /api/admin/customers returns HTTP 200 with every customer's contact name, email, phone, national ID, address and card last-4 to a client account. The spec says only admins may call it (403 for others).
steps: Sign in as acme-1 (a client) over the API
GET /api/admin/customers (see evidence for the exact request)
Observe HTTP 200 with the full customer records, including other companies
actual: HTTP 200 with all customer records (personal data) for all four client accounts
suspected_cause: The route checks that the caller is signed in but not that the role is admin (the sibling /admin/reports/sales does return 403).

regression_test.description: As each client role, GET /api/admin/customers and expect 403

plain.title: Any customer who signs in can see every customer's private details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal and Admin Portal)
plain.what_happens: A customer account can retrieve the full customer list that is meant for staff only, including phone numbers, national ID numbers, addresses and card digits of other companies.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer whose details are stored, and the company's legal and privacy position.
plain.expected: Customer details are visible to staff only; everyone else is refused.

title: A client from one company can open another company's order
summary: GET /api/orders/{id} returns HTTP 200 and the full order to bright-1 (Bright Foods) for an order created by acme-1 (Acme Traders). The order list itself is correctly filtered.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 and POST /api/orders (reference QA-T1), note the returned id
Sign in as bright-1 and GET /api/orders/{id} for that id (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 200 with Acme's order
actual: HTTP 200 with the order body (company name, items, totals)
suspected_cause: Order detail lookup is by id only, with no company ownership check (the list endpoint filters by company).

regression_test.description: Create an order as company A, GET it as company B, expect 403/404

plain.title: A customer can open another company's order if they know its number
plain.where: Client Portal → My orders → an order page (address ending in the order number)
plain.what_happens: Changing the order number in the address bar can show an order that belongs to a different company, including what they bought and the amounts.
plain.expected: A customer only ever sees their own company's orders.

title: Signing out does not end the session
summary: After POST /api/auth/logout returns 204, the same bearer token still gets HTTP 200 from GET /api/me.
steps: Sign in as bright-1 over the API
POST /api/auth/logout and observe 204
GET /api/me with the same token (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 200 instead of 401
suspected_cause: Logout does not revoke the token server-side, despite the spec saying it does.

regression_test.description: Log in, log out, call /me with the same token and expect 401

plain.title: Signing out does not actually end the sign-in
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: After a user signs out, their previous sign-in still works, so anyone who obtained it earlier (for example on a shared computer) keeps access.
plain.who_is_affected: All customers and staff, especially anyone using a shared device.
plain.expected: Signing out ends access at once.

title: Tax is charged on the full amount instead of the discounted amount
summary: For orders with subtotal >= 1,000.00, tax is 10% of the undiscounted subtotal. Subtotal 1000.00: discount 50.00, tax 100.00, total 1050.00 (expected tax 95.00, total 1045.00). Subtotal 1002.00: total 1052.10 (expected 1047.09). Orders under the threshold are right. The UI shows the same wrong total ($1,133.88 for 12 x $89.99; expected $1,128.47).
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with p-101 x2 and p-104 x282 (subtotal 100000 cents)
Observe discount_cents 5000, tax_cents 10000, total_cents 105000; expected tax 9500, total 104500
Repeat with p-101 x5 and p-104 x277 (subtotal 100200): total 105210, expected 104709
actual: tax = 10% of subtotal before discount, so customers are overcharged 5% of the tax base
suspected_cause: Tax is computed from the subtotal rather than subtotal minus discount.

regression_test.description: Orders at 1000.00 and 1002.00 expect total 1045.00 and 1047.09

plain.title: Orders of $1,000 or more are overcharged
plain.where: Client Portal → New order → confirmation message
plain.what_happens: The 5% discount is applied, but the 10% tax is still worked out on the price before the discount, so the total is too high by about 5% of the tax base.
plain.who_is_affected: Every customer placing an order of $1,000 or more, and the company's invoices and sales figures.
how_to_see_it: Sign in to the Client Portal as a customer of Company A
Type a reference starting with QA- in Your PO reference
Choose Printer Toner Cartridge ($89.99) and set the quantity to 12
The green message says the total is $1,133.88; by the stated rules it should be $1,128.47.
plain.expected: Tax is worked out after the discount is taken off.

title: Orders with zero, negative, fractional or over-limit quantities are accepted
summary: POST /api/orders returns 201 for quantity -3 (total -21.45), 0, 1001 and 1.5; the rule and spec say whole numbers 1 to 1000.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with items[0].quantity = -3 (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 201 and total_cents -2145
Repeat for 0, 1001 and 1.5 (baseline probes P044 to P046)
actual: HTTP 201; negative totals appear in the customer's My orders list
suspected_cause: No range or integer check on quantity in the order handler.

plain.title: The system accepts orders with impossible quantities such as minus three
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: An order for a negative, zero, fractional or huge number of items is accepted, producing negative totals that appear in My orders and distort sales figures.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers and staff reading order totals; the company's sales figures.
plain.expected: The order is refused with a clear message.

title: Orders with no items are accepted
summary: POST /api/orders with items: [] returns 201; the rule requires at least one item.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
POST /api/orders with an empty items list (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 201

plain.title: The system accepts orders with nothing in them
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: An empty order can be placed and shows up in order lists.
plain.who_is_affected: Staff processing orders and customers' order history.
plain.expected: An order with no items is refused.

title: Order list fails with an error for page size 0 and for searches containing ( or \
summary: GET /api/orders returns HTTP 500 for page_size=0, q=( and q=\; page_size=-1 returns 200 although the spec minimum is 1.
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
GET /api/orders?page_size=0 (see evidence)
Observe HTTP 500
Repeat with q=( and q=\
expected: HTTP 400 for bad page_size; special characters in q treated as plain text
suspected_cause: Search text is used unescaped in a regular expression; page_size used as a divisor without checking.

regression_test.description: GET orders with page_size=0 and q=( and expect no 5xx

plain.title: Searching orders for certain characters makes the system fail
plain.where: Client Portal → My orders; Admin Portal → Orders (search box)
plain.what_happens: Searching for a bracket or backslash, or unusual page sizes, makes the system fail instead of showing results or a clear message.
plain.expected: Searches work with any characters and bad values get a clear message.

title: Malformed requests return internal technical details
summary: Malformed JSON to POST /api/auth/login and POST /api/orders returns HTTP 400 with a stack trace and server source file paths in the body.
steps: POST /api/auth/login with body {bad (no sign-in needed)
Observe HTTP 400 with stack and file paths (see evidence)
actual: Stack trace and server paths exposed
suspected_cause: Default error handler returns err.stack outside production mode.

regression_test.description: Send malformed JSON and assert the body has no stack or path

plain.title: Error responses reveal internal technical details
plain.where: Behind the screens (the part that talks to the Client Portal)
plain.what_happens: When something unreadable is sent, the system answers with internal details about how it is built, which helps an attacker.
plain.expected: Errors show a short, safe message.

title: Placing the same order twice at once creates duplicate orders
summary: Two identical simultaneous POST /api/orders were both accepted with 201. It is unconfirmed whether the product intends to prevent duplicates, so impact is judged by likely user effect (double-click creating two orders).
steps: Sign in as acme-1 over the API
Send two identical POST /api/orders at the same time (see evidence)
Observe two 201 responses
expected: Duplicates prevented or reference uniqueness enforced

regression_test.description: Send two identical orders concurrently and expect one to be refused

plain.title: A double click can place the same order twice
plain.what_happens: Sending the same order twice at once creates two orders. We did not try a double click on screen.
plain.who_is_affected: Customers who double click and the staff who must cancel extras.
plain.expected: The second copy is refused or flagged.

title: The sales report takes about 4 seconds to load
summary: GET /api/admin/reports/sales consistently takes about 4000 ms (limit 3000 ms) with 25 orders.
steps: Sign in as admin over the API
GET /api/admin/reports/sales (see evidence)
Observe about 4000 ms in repeated runs
suspected_cause: A fixed delay or inefficient aggregation in the report handler.

regression_test.description: Assert the sales report responds in under 3 seconds

plain.title: The sales report is slow to open
plain.what_happens: The report takes about four seconds to appear, and will likely get slower as orders grow.
plain.expected: The report opens within a couple of seconds.
